title: introduce-presubmit-slimliner-and-release-guardrail
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Motivation: reduce presubmit latency and improve release safety by introducing a lightweight presubmit proxy (slimliner) and a release guardrail that verifies dependency anchoring and artifact naming before publishing. Context: teams have been seeing noisy heavyweight linters in CI and occasional release sequencing bugs caused by stale lockfiles or ambiguous artifact names. This PR delivers a small, Go-based presubmit proxy binary (cmd/slimliner) that wraps existing linters/tests to provide: fast AST-level checks, per-package enablement, stderr->structured JSON translation, and an optional in-memory dev cache to speed repeated runs. Additionally, we add a GitHub Actions release guardrail step and a release-checker CLI that runs as part of pre-release jobs to enforce: lockfile freshness (checks transitive freshness against upstream snapshot index), artifact name stamp (semantic prefix + build-hash), and dependency anchoring policy (no unpinned transitive packages on release channel). High-level changes: 1) cmd/slimliner: new Go command with pluggable adapters for eslint, golangci-lint and pytest-quick; adapters live in ./tools/slimliner/adapters. 2) .github/workflows/presubmit-slimline.yml: new fast presubmit lane that runs slimliner on changed packages only. 3) .github/actions/release-guardrail/action.yaml: action that calls the release-checker to validate artifacts and lockfiles before allowing a publish step to proceed. 4) tools/release-checker: small Rust binary that validates artifact naming and queries the internal dependency snapshot API for freshness, with an opt-in local --unsafe-bypass flag for emergency hotfix paths. 5) docs/dev/presubmit.md: onboarding & migration guide for teams to adopt slimliner and opt-in rules. Testing: unit tests for slimliner adapters, smoke tests in GitHub Actions matrix, and an integration test that simulates a stale lockfile to ensure the guardrail halts the release. Migration plan: default presubmit continues to run the full lint/test pipeline for now; presubmit-slimline is opt-in via CODEOWNERS or team-maintainers config. Rollout: opt-in -> team pilot (4 teams) -> org enablement with fallback to full pipeline on a per-repo opt-out. Checklist: - [x] add slimliner CLI and adapters - [x] presubmit workflow and action - [x] release-guardrail action + release-checker binary - [x] docs and migration notes - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] telemetry counters for slimliner run time and guardrail failures Rollout notes: guardrail failure will create a blocking check with actionable message that contains a link to automatic remediation scripts (scripts/lockfile-refresh). Related: ENG-1892 (presubmit performance), ENG-2043 (release stability). Security: release-checker contacts internal snapshot API over mTLS and respects configured service account roles. Backout: remove new workflows and action entries from the repo, or set PRESUBMIT_SLIMLINE=false in repo settings to revert to legacy presubmit behavior. Impact: expected median presubmit latency reduction for typical change sets: 45-60%, with minimal false-positive risk since slimliner only runs fast, mechanical checks by default. Release guardrail prevents a class of broken releases tied to unpinned transitive dependencies and ambiguous artifact names. See release_notes for details.

discussion: Evelyn: Looks promising; a couple asks: 1) can slimliner be compiled into a tiny docker image for self-hosted runners? 2) ensure adapters fail open for non-critical checks so we don't block merges for flaky linters. Priya: Answered: slimliner is compiled statically and we add a small Dockerfile in this PR; adapters default to 'non-blocking' by config and presubmit-slimline marks them as advisory unless repo config flips 'enforce=true'. Troy: Request: Add telemetry tag for 'team' so we can roll out per-team. Priya: Added telemetry tag and an opt-in config piece in docs. Samir: Concern about release-checker making network calls in Actions and slowing release. Priya: release-checker caches snapshot index for 30s and runs in parallel; observed ~120ms median in smoke tests. Samir: Approves after perf numbers. Final: 2 approvals, CI green, squash+merge performed.
release_notes: Added a lightweight presubmit proxy (slimliner) to speed up fast feedback loops and a release guardrail action to block publishing on stale lockfiles or unpinned transitive deps. Opt-in presubmit lane for teams with migration docs and a rollout plan. Includes telemetry and remediation scripts.
notes_for_reviewers: Please focus review on adapters (eslint/golangci/pytest) and the release-guardrail action integration. Verify the emergency --unsafe-bypass path is gated behind a repo-level setting and audit logs are emitted when used. See docs/dev/presubmit.md for configuration examples.
postmerge_tasks: 1) Monitor slimliner.run_time telemetry and guardrail.failure reasons for first 2 weeks 2) Run org pilot with 4 teams and collect false-positive counts 3) Schedule follow-up to add ruby/scala adapters if pilot metrics are satisfactory
